verifications.claim: SpaceX is not directly involved in the flight hardware or launch of the Artemis II mission
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'why isn’t SpaceX launching astronauts around the Moon on Artemis II? ... Artemis II ... is built around NASA’s Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and the Orion crew capsule.'; R5: 'Artemis II ... first crewed test flight of SLS and Orion.'; R1: 'a crewed Orion spacecraft that will be launched from Earth by a NASA Space Launch System (SLS) launcher.'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm Artemis II uses SLS/Orion, not SpaceX hardware or launch.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission uses NASA’s own Space Launch System (SLS) rocket
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Artemis II ... is built around NASA’s Space Launch System (SLS) rocket'; R5: 'The crew will launch aboard SLS/Orion'; R1: 'NASA Space Launch System (SLS) launcher.'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated in sources that Artemis II launches on SLS.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission uses Orion capsule
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Orion crew capsule'; R5: 'first crewed flight of the Orion spacecraft'; R1: 'crewed Orion spacecraft'.
verifications.reasoning: All relevant sources explicitly state Orion for Artemis II.

verifications.claim: SpaceX has been awarded contracts to develop the Starship Human Landing System (HLS) for future missions, specifically Artemis III
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'NASA awarded SpaceX a contract ... Starship HLS ... for the Artemis III mission (subsequently delayed)'; R2: 'NASA selected SpaceX’s Starship Human Landing System (HLS) ... during Artemis III'; R4: 'SpaceX has a contract to develop their Starship HLS for use on Artemis III and Artemis IV.'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm SpaceX contract for Starship HLS originally for Artemis III, even if delayed.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is a crewed lunar flyby (no landing)
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'four astronauts on a lunar flyby ... does not require a lunar lander'; R5: 'Crewed lunar flyby ... free-return trajectory around the Moon'; R3: 'NASA’s Artemis II crew completed a historic lunar flyby'.
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly describe Artemis II as crewed flyby with no landing.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R5: 'Artemis II (April 1, 2026)'; R3: context implies 2026 completion; R2: pre-launch reference to upcoming Artemis II.
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm scheduling and occurrence in 2026.

verifications.claim: Artemis II uses legacy SLS/Orion systems to test deep-space habitation and navigation
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R2: 'crewed test of SLS and Orion in deep space, essentially validating NASA’s own system'; R5: 'validate the Orion spacecraft's systems, crew operations ... testing of the spacecraft in high Earth orbit ... lunar flyby'; SLS/Orion described as legacy Shuttle-derived.
verifications.reasoning: SLS/Orion confirmed as legacy; tests deep-space systems including implicitly habitation/navigation, but not precisely phrased as such.

verifications.claim: SpaceX is contracted to provide the Starship HLS to land astronauts on the Moon starting with the Artemis III mission
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R5: 'Artemis III ... test rendezvous and docking tests in Earth orbit with ... Starship HLS'; 'Artemis IV ... first lunar landing'; R1: 'for the Artemis III mission (subsequently delayed by NASA until Artemis IV)'
verifications.reasoning: Contract exists, but landing delayed; Artemis III now Earth orbit test only, landing starts Artemis IV.
